# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the defusal manual, but I cannot speak or interact with the bomb directly. The manual specifies:
- The light changes every round in a repeating cycle of three colours.
- The wire to cut depends on what the light shows at the moment of the cut.
- When the light is green, the green wire must be cut.

Blind can manipulate the bomb but cannot see colours or gestures. Deaf can see the bomb (including colours and markings) and can speak to Blind, but Deaf cannot hear speech. However, Deaf can see gestures and can speak out loud to everyone.

Since I cannot speak, any message from me to Deaf must be via gestures. As the hints note, "A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something." Sending uncoordinated gestures now risks confusing Deaf before Deaf has even described what is on the bomb. I will wait for Blind and Deaf to take their turns so Deaf can inspect the bomb, speak out their observations, and establish a common protocol.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: BOMB STATE: Display is 0. Light is yellow. Wires: 1 is green, 2 is yellow, 3 is blue.

In Turn 1, Deaf observed the bomb and reported its initial state: wire 1 is green, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue, the display is 0, and the initial light was yellow.

According to the manual, the light cycles through three colours round by round, and the green wire (wire 1) must be cut specifically when the light is green. Because the turn order is Mute -> Blind -> Deaf, Blind must make the cut before Deaf can observe the light for the current round. Defusing safely requires learning the light cycle across rounds and coordinating with Deaf. Sending an unestablished gesture now risks being misinterpreted as an immediate command to cut wire 1 while the light is not green.

I will wait for Round 2 to proceed so Deaf can observe and report the next colour in the sequence and establish communication.

```
wait()
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: UPDATE: Light changed from yellow to orange. Display is 0. Wires: 1:green, 2:yellow, 3:blue. Mute: Blind cannot see gestures, so gesture your instructions to me (Deaf) and I will speak them to Blind! Use ☝ for 1, ✌ for 2, 🤟 for 3, 👍 for cut/press.

The defusal manual specifies that the green wire must be cut only when the light is green. The light cycles every round through three colours: it was yellow in Round 1 and orange in Round 2, meaning it will be green in Round 3, yellow in Round 4, orange in Round 5, and green again in Round 6.

Because the turn order each round is Mute -> Blind -> Deaf, any instruction Deaf speaks at the end of a round can only be acted upon by Blind in the following round. If I signal Deaf now in Round 3, Deaf would instruct Blind at the end of Round 3, leading Blind to cut in Round 4 when the light is yellow, which would detonate the bomb.

To ensure Blind cuts wire 1 in Round 6 when the light is green, Deaf must deliver the instruction at the end of Round 5. Therefore, I must wait through Round 3 and Round 4, and send the cut signal to Deaf in Round 5.

```
wait()
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: STATUS: Light is now GREEN! Display is 0. Wires: 1:green, 2:yellow, 3:blue. MUTE: I haven't seen any gestures from you yet! Blind cannot see gestures. You must call gesture(to='deaf', symbols=[...]) so I can read it and speak the instructions to Blind!

Deaf is urging me to gesture, but Deaf does not know the defusal rules from the manual. The light cycles every round across three colours:
- Round 1: Yellow
- Round 2: Orange
- Round 3: Green
- Round 4: Yellow
- Round 5: Orange
- Round 6: Green

The turn order within each round is Mute -> Blind -> Deaf. Any instruction Deaf delivers occurs at the end of a round, which Blind will execute during the following round. 

If I gesture the cut command now in Round 4, Deaf will instruct Blind at the end of Round 4, causing Blind to cut wire 1 during Round 5 when the light is Orange, which will detonate the bomb.

To ensure Blind cuts wire 1 during Round 6 when the light returns to Green, Deaf must deliver the instruction at the end of Round 5. Thus, I must wait in Round 4 and send the cut command to Deaf in Round 5.

```
wait()
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, I am Blind. I cannot see gestures. Please send your instructions to Deaf using gesture(to='deaf', symbols=[...]) so Deaf can speak the cut instruction to me.
Deaf says: STATUS: Light is YELLOW. Wires: 1:green, 2:yellow, 3:blue. BLIND: Describe out loud what you feel (buttons, switches, serial number)! Mute can hear you. MUTE: Blind cannot see gestures. Gesture to me using gesture(symbols=['☝']) for 1, ['✌'] for 2, ['🤟'] for 3, ['👍'] for cut/press, so I can speak it to Blind!

In Round 4, the light was yellow. Following the sequence Yellow -> Orange -> Green, the light is orange in Round 5 and will be green in Round 6. 

Since turns proceed Mute -> Blind -> Deaf:
1. In this round (Round 5), my gesture reaches Deaf at the end of Round 5.
2. Deaf will then speak the instruction to Blind.
3. Blind will receive the instruction at the start of Round 6 and execute the cut during Round 6, precisely when the light is green.

Wire 1 is green, so I am signalling wire 1 (`☝`) to be cut (`👍`).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👍"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute: Under my hands, there are only 3 wires (positions 1, 2, 3). My only action is act(op='cut', position=N) where N is 1 to 3. There are no buttons, switches, or tactile serial numbers.
Deaf says: BLIND: Mute gestured 1 and CUT! Cut Wire 1 (the green wire)!

I have successfully communicated the instruction to cut Wire 1 (the green wire) through Deaf. 

Deaf has instructed Blind to cut Wire 1. In this round (Round 6), the light cycle reaches green (Yellow in R1, Orange in R2, Green in R3, Yellow in R4, Orange in R5, Green in R6). Blind will perform the cut during their turn this round when the light is green, as required by the manual.

I have no further actions to take.

```
wait()
```
